title: "Static scattering area"
format:

How far the local scattering area $A$ changes between acquisitions of one relative
orbit, i.e. what a static $A$ (one per relative orbit, as for OPERA RTC-S1) would get
wrong, from one mountainous burst footprint over all acquisitions of the compositing
windows 2015–2025 (2026 is not fully processed). Terrain flattening divides by $A$ and
local resolution weighting weights by $1/A$, so the error of a static $A$ is the same in
both, in dB: $\varepsilon_t = 10 \log_{10}(A_t / A_\text{static})$. $A_\text{static}$
is the per-pixel temporal median, the best any static value can do, and each pixel is
summarised by its worst acquisition. 1 dB is Sentinel-1's specified absolute radiometric
accuracy (3σ; Schmidt et al., 2018, 2020). Where the LRW weight cap
(`clip_max_resolution`) sits in the distribution of $1/A$ is in `lrw-weight-cap.qmd`.

Radar shadow is NaN in the products and is left out of each pixel's statistics; a
last section counts the pixels that change between shadow and observed. The analysed
area is inside the footprint of every acquisition.

```{python}
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
import warnings

import numpy as np
from rasterio.windows import Window
from scipy import ndimage
import yaml

from freezebase.raster import rasterio_open

from glace_production.config import settings
from data_paths import LRW_CONFIG, run_dirs
```

## Configuration

Burst 30346 of IW1 on relative orbit 15 covers the Bernese Alps, Valais and Ticino, the
footprint of an earlier analysis of the static terrain flattening.

```{python}
BURST = "015A_030346_IW1"  # relative orbit and pass, burst ID, sub-swath
POLARIZATION = "VV"  # VV and VH products carry the same scattering area
YEARS = range(2015, 2025 + 1)
AREA_BAND = 2  # band 1 is gamma0, band 2 the scattering area
THRESHOLD_DB = 1.0
BLOCK_ROWS = 256  # rows read at once, from every acquisition
N_WORKERS = 8

WEIGHT_CAP = yaml.safe_load(LRW_CONFIG.read_text())["clip_max_resolution"]
CAP_DB = 10 * np.log10(WEIGHT_CAP)  # A is capped below -CAP_DB

files = sorted(
    (
        f
        for year in YEARS
        for f in run_dirs(year).prod_dir.glob(f"S1_RTC_{BURST}_{POLARIZATION}_*.tif")
    ),
    key=lambda f: f.name,
)
print(f"{len(files)} acquisitions")
```

## Statistics

The acquisitions share one 10 m grid; each is placed on the union of their extents.

```{python}
bounds = []
for f in files:
    with rasterio_open(f) as src:
        bounds.append((src.bounds, src.res[0], src.height, src.width))
res = bounds[0][1]
left = min(b.left for b, *_ in bounds)
top = max(b.top for b, *_ in bounds)
width = round((max(b.right for b, *_ in bounds) - left) / res)
height = round((top - min(b.bottom for b, *_ in bounds)) / res)
offsets = [(round((top - b.top) / res), round((b.left - left) / res)) for b, *_ in bounds]


def read_rows(i: int, start: int, stop: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Scattering area of acquisition ``i`` in rows ``start:stop`` of the union grid."""
    out = np.full((stop - start, width), np.nan, dtype="float32")
    (r, c), (_, _, h, w) = offsets[i], bounds[i]
    lo, hi = max(start - r, 0), min(stop - r, h)
    if lo < hi:
        with rasterio_open(files[i]) as src:
            out[lo + r - start : hi + r - start, c : c + w] = src.read(
                AREA_BAND, window=Window(0, lo, w, hi - lo)
            )
    return out


def footprint(i: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Pixels inside the footprint of acquisition ``i``, shadow holes filled."""
    return ndimage.binary_fill_holes(np.isfinite(read_rows(i, 0, height)))


area = np.ones((height, width), dtype=bool)
with ThreadPoolExecutor(N_WORKERS) as ex:
    for fp in ex.map(footprint, range(len(files))):
        area &= fp
print(f"analysed area {area.sum() * res**2 / 1e6:.0f} km²")
```

Per pixel: the worst deviation from the temporal median, the temporal standard
deviation of $\varepsilon_t$, the smallest valid $A$, the number of valid acquisitions
and how often the pixel changes between valid and shadow from one acquisition to the
next (in date order).

```{python}
worst_db = np.full((height, width), np.nan, dtype="float32")
std_db = np.full((height, width), np.nan, dtype="float32")
min_db = np.full((height, width), np.nan, dtype="float32")
n_valid = np.zeros((height, width), dtype="uint16")
n_switch = np.zeros((height, width), dtype="uint16")

with ThreadPoolExecutor(N_WORKERS) as ex, warnings.catch_warnings():
    warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)  # all-NaN pixels outside the area
    for start in range(0, height, BLOCK_ROWS):
        stop = min(start + BLOCK_ROWS, height)
        stack = np.stack(list(ex.map(lambda i: read_rows(i, start, stop), range(len(files)))))
        stack[:, ~area[start:stop]] = np.nan
        db = 10 * np.log10(np.where(stack > 0, stack, np.nan))
        del stack
        eps = db - np.nanmedian(db, axis=0)
        worst_db[start:stop] = np.nanmax(np.abs(eps), axis=0)
        std_db[start:stop] = np.nanstd(eps, axis=0)
        min_db[start:stop] = np.nanmin(db, axis=0)
        valid = np.isfinite(db)
        n_valid[start:stop] = valid.sum(0)
        n_switch[start:stop] = (valid[1:] != valid[:-1]).sum(0)  # files are in date order
        del db, eps, valid
```

## Results

Pixels need two valid acquisitions for a deviation.

```{python}
pixels = area & (n_valid >= 2)
worst = worst_db[pixels]
print(
    f"{np.mean(worst > THRESHOLD_DB):.1%} of the pixels deviate by more than "
    f"{THRESHOLD_DB:g} dB from their temporal median A in at least one of "
    f"{len(files)} acquisitions (median pixel {np.median(worst):.2f} dB)."
)
```

For comparison with Agram et al. (2023), who report the temporal standard deviation of
the flattening factor of a Sentinel-1 burst stack processed with SNAP:

```{python}
print(f"temporal std below 0.1 dB: {np.mean(std_db[pixels] < 0.1):.1%} of the pixels")
```

## Shadow

The deviations above leave out the acquisitions in which a pixel has no valid $A$,
radar shadow. How many pixels of the analysed area are in shadow in some acquisitions
and observed in others, and how often they change. Pixels that are never shadowed
change zero times; the smallest valid $A$ of a switching pixel tells whether it borders
shadow on the high-resolution side ($A$ below the weight cap) or not.

```{python}
nv, ns = n_valid[area], n_switch[area]
switching = (nv > 0) & (nv < len(files))
print(f"never shadowed: {np.mean(nv == len(files)):.2%} of the area")
print(f"always shadowed: {np.mean(nv == 0):.2%}")
print(f"shadowed in some acquisitions, observed in others: {np.mean(switching):.2%}")
print(
    f"changes between shadow and observed per switching pixel: median "
    f"{np.median(ns[switching]):.0f}, 90th percentile {np.quantile(ns[switching], 0.9):.0f} "
    f"(of {len(files) - 1} possible)"
)
shadowed = len(files) - nv[switching]
print(
    f"acquisitions in shadow per switching pixel: median {np.median(shadowed):.0f}, "
    f"10th-90th percentile {np.quantile(shadowed, 0.1):.0f}-{np.quantile(shadowed, 0.9):.0f}"
)
near = min_db[area][switching] < -CAP_DB
print(f"switching pixels with smallest valid A < {1 / WEIGHT_CAP:g}: {np.mean(near):.1%}")
```
